text: As the latest crop of students pen their undergraduate application form and weigh up their options, it may be worth considering just how the point, purpose and value of a degree has changed and what Generation Z need to consider as they start the third stage of their educational journey.
translation: 随着最新一批年轻学子纷纷提笔填写本科入学申请表并权衡各自的人生抉择，当下的确非常值得深入思考：大学学位的真正意义、宗旨与价值究竟发生了何种深刻转变，以及 Z 世代（Generation Z）在开启其第三阶段求学生涯时究竟需要审慎考量些什么（reassess necessity of college education）。

text: Millennials were told that if you did well in school, got a decent degree, you would be set up for life. But that promise has been found wanting. As degrees became universal, they became devalued. Education was no longer a secure route of social mobility.
translation: 千禧一代（Millennials）曾被长辈告知：只要在学校成绩优异、拿下一张体面的大学文凭，就能一生衣食无忧、立于不败之地。然而，这一美好的承诺如今已被证明大打折扣、漏洞百出。随着大学文凭走向普及化泛滥，其含金量也随之严重贬值（devalued）；高等教育再也不是一条稳妥通畅的社会阶层上升流动通道。

text: Today, 28 percent of graduates in the UK are in non-graduate roles, a percentage which is double the average among the OECD countries.
translation: 在当今英国，高达28%的大学毕业生在从事根本不需要本科学历的低阶岗位（non-graduate roles），这一比例甚至是经合组织（OECD）国家平均水平的整整两倍（reflects the shrinking value of a degree）。

text: This is not to say that there is no point in getting a degree, but rather stress that a degree is not for everyone, that the switch from classroom to lecture hall is not an inevitable one and that other options are available.
translation: 这绝不是说攻读大学学位毫无意义，而是强调大学学位并不适合所有人；从中学教室直接迈入大学阶梯讲堂绝非唯一不可避免的必然路径，人生完全还有其他切实可行的替代选择。

text: Thankfully, there are signs that this is already happening, with Generation Z seeking to learn from their millennial predecessors, even if parents and teachers tend to be still set in the degree mindset.
translation: 令人欣慰的是，有诸多迹象表明这种务实转变已经悄然发生：Z 世代正主动从千禧一代前人的挫折中汲取深刻教训，哪怕许多家长和教师的思想观念依然顽固禁锢在非拿文凭不可的旧思维定式之中。

text: Employers have long seen the advantages of hiring school leavers who often prove themselves to be more committed and loyal employees than graduates. Many too are seeing the advantages of scrapping a degree requirement for certain roles.
translation: 广大雇主早已敏锐洞察到了直接录用中学毕业生（school leavers）的显著优势——事实证明，他们往往比大学毕业生更具敬业投入度与企业忠诚度；许多雇主同样深刻体会到了对特定岗位彻底取消文凭硬性要求的巨大好处（employers taking realistic attitude to degrees）。

text: For those for whom a degree is the desired route, consider that this may well be the first of many. In this age of generalists, it pays to have specific knowledge or skills. Postgraduates now earn 40 percent more than graduates. When more and more of us have a degree, it makes sense to have two.
translation: 对于那些确实将攻读学位视作理想道路的人而言，请清醒意识到这很可能只是你未来众多学位的起点。在这个充斥着普通通才的时代，唯有掌握极其深度的专门知识或技能才能获得丰厚回报（further studies in a specific field）。如今研究生的平均收入比普通本科生高出整整40%；当身边的大学本科生越来越泛滥时，拥有两张文凭才真正合乎情理。

text: It is unlikely that Generation Z will be done with education at 18 or 21; they will need to be constantly up-skilling throughout their career to stay employable. It has been estimated that this generation, due to the pressures of technology, the wish for personal fulfilment and desire for diversity, will work for 17 different employers over the course of their working life and have five different careers. Education, and not just knowledge gained on campus, will be a core part of Generation Z's career trajectory.
translation: Z 世代绝不可能在18岁或21岁大学毕业时就宣告教育的彻底终结；为了终身保持核心就业竞争力，他们将必须在整个职业生涯中持续不断地进行技能迭代升级（constantly up-skilling / lifelong learning）。据权威预测，出于科技变革重压、个人价值实现以及对多元体验的渴望，这一代人一生中平均将为17家不同的雇主效力，并跨界涉足5种完全不同的职业。贯穿一生的学习教育——而远非仅仅局限于校园内所习得的书本知识——将成为 Z 世代职业人生轨迹的绝对核心支柱（Lifelong learning will define them）。

text: Older generations often talk about their degree in the present and personal tense: "I am a geographer" or "I am a classicist". Their sons or daughters would never say such a thing; it's as if they already know that their degree won't define them in the same way.
translation: 老一辈人谈起自己的大学文凭时，往往喜欢使用第一人称现在时：“我是一名地理学者”或“我是一名古典学家”。然而他们的年轻儿女们绝不会再说出这般言语——仿佛他们早已深切洞悉：大学文凭再也无法以同样僵化的方式去定义他们绚烂广阔的人生轨迹。
